title: Licorice root decoction for dry cough
subtitle: A soothing decoction of Glycyrrhiza glabra root for dry, irritated coughs and inflamed airways
excerpt: Licorice root decoction is a 15-minute simmer of dried Glycyrrhiza glabra root in water, strained and taken warm for dry, irritated coughs and scratchy inflamed throat. The root is rich in glycyrrhizin and mucilaginous polysaccharides that coat and soothe the airway lining. One cup up to three times a day for short courses. Not for use beyond 4 to 6 weeks or in people with high blood pressure. Sweet, earthy, intensely liquorice-flavoured.

glossaryTerms.definition: A herb or preparation rich in mucilage that soothes and coats inflamed or irritated mucous membranes, airways, throat, digestive tract. Demulcents reduce the irritation that drives a dry cough by physically coating the inflamed surface.

The primary active constituent of licorice root, a triterpenoid saponin that is responsible for both its anti-inflammatory and expectorant actions, and for its well-documented effects on blood pressure and potassium levels at high or extended doses.
A preparation made by simmering dried plant material (root, bark, seed) in water for 10-20 minutes, then straining. Used for woody plant parts that need longer extraction than a simple infusion.

content.text: Licorice root
decoction
is dried Glycyrrhiza glabra root simmered in water for 15 minutes, strained warm into a mug, and drunk slowly for a dry, scratchy, irritated cough. A classic
demulcent
, the root's gel-rich polysaccharides coat the inflamed airway lining and the
glycyrrhizin
reduces the inflammatory irritation that drives the cough reflex. The
decoction

is intensely sweet and earthy, the most identifiably liquorice-flavoured of all herbal teas. Good for dry, unproductive post-cold coughs and the scratchy throat of the first day of illness. Not for prolonged use.

attrs.title: Precautions, read before using
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Ingredients
Method
Place 5 g of dried licorice root in a small saucepan with 250 ml of cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes. The liquid will reduce slightly and darken to a warm amber.
Strain through a fine strainer into a mug. Allow to cool to a comfortable drinking temperature before sipping. Drink slowly to maximise contact time with the throat.
Dosing
One cup up to three times a day. Use for a maximum of 2 weeks for a seasonal cough. consult a herbalist for longer courses in chronic airway conditions.
Storage
Dried licorice root stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Decoct each cup fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you have hypertension, kidney disease, oedema, or take cardiac or diuretic medication. See a doctor for a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, a cough with blood, or any cough accompanied by unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or chest pain.
